steps.text: Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease and flour a 10-inch bundt pan.
Beat butter and sugar together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Beat one egg at a time into the butter mixture; add lemon extract with last egg.
Sift together the flour, baking soda and salt. Alternately mix in the flour mixture and the yogurt, starting and ending with the dry ingredients. Beat just until incorporated.

Pour batter into prepared pan. Bake in the preheated oven for 60 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean. Allow to cool 10 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a wire rack and cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Yogurt Cake
raw_recipe.description: A lemon pound cake made with yogurt instead of sour cream.

review.reviewBody: My family really enjoyed this cake. It is very moist. We cut down the sugar by 1/4 and added an egg to make up for it. We didnt have margarine so we just used vegetable oil instead. We used vannila extract and vanilla yogurt instead of lemon.

I enjoy baking breads and cakes for my husband to have in the morning with his coffee. I have been testing recipes in my Ninja Cooker in preparation for a long road trip in the RV, and decided to give this a go.

Changes made were:
1 cup of sugar instead of 2
1 cup of coconut flour and 1 cup of regular cake flour
Plain yogurt instead of flavored
The juice of 3 meyer lemons and lemon zest from our garden
1 tsp. of real vanilla

I preheated the cooker for 325, poured the batter right in, and baked for 1 hour. The bottom was a little darker than I would like, but the cake was perfectly moist and very lemony. Next time I will lower temperature to 300 degrees and bake it a little longer.

Delicious. Not overly sweet. I was worried that it might be too sweet but I went ahead and followed recipe exactly. Even the baking time was right on the money. Next time I will add an extra teaspoon of lemon extract along with lots of poppy seeds. I will note that I used Chobani Lemon Yogurt. The packages say 5.3 ounces. Good thing I measured becase as it turns out they actually contain 4.5 ounces in the pacakage as measured with the Pyrex 5 ounce liquid measure cup. It took just shy of two packages of the yogurt. *(This recipe calls for butter and when I read some of the reviews it sounded like people thought it called for margarine. I wonder if it called for margarine and then was later edited. I would never use margarine anyways but I found that curious.) - Thanks for sharing.

I made a few alterations to suit my needs: I cut out 1/2c of sugar as others suggested, I made it into cupcakes, I used Greek yogurt because it's what I had on hand, and I replaced the lemon with vanilla. They turned out fabulous. 1/4 cup batter in each wrapper yielded cupcakes with beautiful golden domes just above the top of the wrapper, they cooked all the way through and had a perfect texture. I am serving them with a drizzle of Martha Stewart's Caramel Bourbon Vanilla sauce (http://www.marthastewart.com/338951/caramel-bourbon-vanilla-sauce?center=0&gallery=274972&slide=199286). I will certainly make these again.
So good! Only took 50 minutes when I baked in 2 loaf pans. I used greek vanilla yogurt and added a touch more lemon extract. Super moist! Served with strawberries and whipped cream

I used 1 cup whole wheat pastry flour, 1 cup unbleached, 1/4 less sugar, vanilla yogurt, and lemon peel instead of almond extract, and it came out great! We live at 9,000 feet so used only 1-1/4 tsp. baking powder and slightly less than 1/2 tsp. baking soda. Upped the oven temp to 360° to help it set up faster so it didn't fall too, cooking it 5 min. less than recipe says. Put the juice from the lemon and confectioner's sugar together to drizzle on top. Excellent!!!

Very easy and delicious recipe! We reduced the sugar by a 1/2 cup and thought it was perfect. I also used Butter flavored margarine to keep the fat and calorie count down. I didn't have lemon yogurt, so I used low fat yogurt 1 tbsp of lemon juice and the zest of 1 lemon in the recipe. I also made a syrup glaze for the top (made it in a square 9x9 pan and a few small petit four size cakes) The glaze was 1/4 cup of lemon juice, zest of 1 lemon, and 1/4 cup of sugar, brought to a simmer on the stove. It it was reduced and glaze consistency. I let the cake cool in the pan, then when it was just barely still warm. I pricked the top with a fork, and brushed the glaze on slowly bit by bit, so everything had time to soak in. It is by far one of the most delicious, and refreshing deserts ever. Next time I might reduce the sugar another half cup and sub splenda. A very yummy treat!

Yum. I'm giving 4 stars because I didn't like the recipe as much the way it's written. I followed another reviewer's suggestion of using 1 cup of sugar and vanilla Greek yogurt. I also zested a lemon in place of the lemon extract and it was wonderful. My whole house smelled of warm lemony goodness. I also don't recommend banning for a whole hour. Mine was ready to come out of the oven at 50 min.

I cut the sugar to 1 1/2 cups, added a 4th egg, used butter instead of margarine, and used whole milk greek plain yogurt.

I combined the sugar with the grated zest of two oranges and let is sit overnight to really infuse.

I used 1/2 teast vanilla, and 1/2 teas orange extract.

Turned out great. Nice and moist with a mild orange flavor.

This cake is delicious, moist, and full of flavour! I added 2 cups of fresh cranberries, which made it taste exactly like the muffins Costco used to bake. This recipe was a huge hit in my family. Everyone loved it!!

As written , I give a 4 star . Second time I made it I used fat free Greek yogurt , doubled the lemon extract , add zest and juice of a lemon - and it was 5 star quality. Cooked in 50 minutes in my oven . I don’t recommend using less butter or sugar as suggested by others. This is cake . If you want less fat , eat vegetables.

Fantastic! A slight crunch on outside, super light and fluffy inside. Like some others, I used 1/2 butter and 1/2 olive oil; added lemon juice and rind; and, used plain whole milk yogurt (homemade!) instead of lemon yogurt. Also drizzled on icing sugar mixed with lemons rind juice. DEFINITELY MAKING AGAIN! 🤩

I have baked this a few times,every time I have extra yogurt on hand. I did not have lemon yogurt, but nonfat plain yogurt. I lessened the sugar by 1/2 cup, added a tablespoon of lemon juice and zest of one lemon. I baked it for 50 minutes at 325. Just perfect, not too sweet, light and spongy. This is my only go to yogurt recipe.Thank you.

I use vanilla whole milk Greek yogurt instead of lemon yogurt, and (because I don't like lemon extract) I juice a whole lemon to use with confectioners sugar for a glaze, and zest the top. It's a warmer, brighter flavor and pairs beautifully with fresh berries.
Haven’t made this yet but want to, was wondering what the best pan is to use from those of you who have made it—just trying to find out the general opinion. Thanks!

I made it using vanilla extract and whole milk yogurt, and added a teaspoon of lemon juice. It didn't come out of the pan in one piece, but I think that's my fault, not the recipe's. I was a little confused as to when the flour+yogurt mixture was to be combined with the other ingredients. It tastes absolutely amazing, though and I want to try to make it again.
First time making this and it was delicious! Everybody I gave a piece to said it was great! Next time, I'm going to add some lemon glaze over the top.

This Bundt cake is delicious, moist, full of flavor, and easy to make! Changes: I used plain Greek yogurt and fresh lemon juice from a whole lemon and lemon zest from another lemon. That’s it! Definitely I will make it again and again.

I halved the recipe since I did not want to end up with 2 loaves of cake I didn’t like (I don’t have a Bundt pan). I did slightly cut back on the sugar and used 2 eggs and 4 oz of plain whole milk yogurt . I didn’t have lemon extract but had lemons so I used juice of 1/2 lemon and zest of a whole lemon. It came out very good! I should’ve used juice of the whole lemon (I like lemon flavor!) and cut back on sugar even more (although rest of the family thought it was perfectly sweet). My only complaint was that it didn’t rise as much as I had hoped. But the slight flatness was a fine trade off for the taste and texture of a cake.
Perfect, delicious, foolproof recipe! So easy, even I can make it! Instantly brought me back to my childhood in France... It's the first cake we learned how to make as kids.
